text: Coca-Cola once wanted a new American coin.
For decades, a bottle of Coke cost just five cents.
But by 1950, Coca-Cola had around 400,000 vending machines.
Most were built for one coin.
Raise the price to six cents? Customers needed extra change.
Raise it to ten? That's DOUBLE.
So Coke came up with a wild idea.
What if America made a seven-and-a-half-cent coin?
In 1953, Coke's powerful chairman reportedly took the idea to President Eisenhower.
Most companies change their prices to fit the money.
Coca-Cola tried to change the money to fit its price.
